mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of >1% INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous and CPIAUCSL > 202 (index) for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their previous values and CPIAUCSL > 202 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K units for four consecutive months signals a weakening residential construction sector, which reduces demand for materials and related equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below 900K for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months indicates a paradoxical labor market signal, often preceding a sharp correction; this predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE increases simultaneously over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real personal savings (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over a 5-day horizon, as increased household savings raise the potential for future consumption and investment, supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS growth is positive.
